stories.title: Why the Sky Wears Blue
body: Little Anaya loved looking at the sky. One evening she asked her grandmother, "Dadi, why is the sky blue in the day but orange at sunset?" Dadi smiled and said, "Let the Sunbeam tell you himself."

That night, a friendly Sunbeam appeared in Anaya's dream. "Hello Anaya! I travel all the way from the Sun. My white light is actually made of seven colours hidden together — red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo, and violet!"

"When I enter the sky," the Sunbeam continued, "I bump into tiny bits of air. The blue part of me bounces and scatters all around the sky much more than the other colours. That is why you see the sky filled with blue!"

"But at sunset," said the Sunbeam, "I have to travel through much more air to reach you. By then, most of the blue has scattered away, and the red and orange colours reach your eyes. That is why sunsets glow orange and pink!"

Anaya woke up amazed. Now every time she looked at the sky, she remembered that its colours were made of dancing light and tiny bits of air. Science, she realized, was the most wonderful magic of all — and it was real!

quiz.q: How many colours are hidden in white light?
Which colour scatters most in the sky?
Why is the sky blue in the day?

opts: Blue scatters away, red reaches us

quiz.q: What did Anaya think science was?
